### Math Basics Demonstration

The quadratic formula provides the solutions to a quadratic equation of the form \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\). In inline notation, it is written as $x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$, where the discriminant \(b^2 - 4ac\) determines the nature of the roots.

Here is a system of linear equations displayed with alignment:
$$\begin{align}
x + y &= 5 \\
2x - y &= 1
\end{align}$$

The identity matrix and a piecewise function can be represented as:
$$I = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}, \quad
f(x) = \begin{cases}
x^2 & \text{if } x \geq 0 \\
-x & \text{if } x < 0
\end{cases}$$

Some fundamental equations in physics and geometry include:
$$E = mc^2$$
$$F = ma$$
$$a^2 + b^2 = c^2$$

See [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadratic_formula) for more details on the quadratic formula.
